title: Exact Boolean multiplicative complexity of four-term polynomial multiplication
abstract: Proves that multiplying two binary polynomials with n coefficients needs exactly 0, 1, 3, 6, and 9 AND gates for n = 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, with XOR and constants free and arbitrary reuse of earlier nonlinear wires. The main lower bound excludes every eight-gate circuit for n = 4. Develops Boolean algebraic normal forms equivalent to all Boolean functions, a general circuit model, dimension bounds, circuit rewiring, a Reed-Muller minimum-weight theorem, and exterior-algebra and jet arguments controlling nonlinear feedback.

informal.UnrestrictedBooleanMul.mc_mul_zero: The empty polynomial multiplication map needs zero AND gates.
informal.UnrestrictedBooleanMul.mc_mul_one: Multiplying two one-coefficient binary polynomials needs exactly one AND gate.
informal.UnrestrictedBooleanMul.mc_mul_two: Multiplying two two-coefficient binary polynomials needs exactly three AND gates.
informal.UnrestrictedBooleanMul.mc_mul_three: Multiplying two three-coefficient binary polynomials needs exactly six AND gates.
informal.UnrestrictedBooleanMul.N4.mc_mul_four: Multiplying two four-coefficient binary polynomials needs exactly nine AND gates, allowing free XOR, constants, and unrestricted nonlinear reuse.
informal.UnrestrictedBooleanMul.N4.no_eight_gate_: No eight-AND circuit with free XOR, constants, and arbitrary nonlinear reuse computes all seven output coefficients of the product of two four-coefficient binary polynomials.
